input.quote: (f) actual or alleged infringement of any Third Party's Intellectual Property by the Product or by either Party in performing its duties or obligations hereunder with respect to the Product;
input.rationale: The Agreement contains mutual indemnities with standard procedure (notice, control of defence, participation, settlement, cooperation at §§ 12.2.1–12.2.5), but the third-party IP infringement risk runs one way against us. SFJ's indemnity at § 12.1.1 (p0687–p0691) covers only gross negligence/wilful misconduct, material breach of the Agreement, Protocol or AZ License, and post-Program-Transfer trial injury and product liability — it contains no third-party IP infringement limb. By contrast, our indemnity at § 12.1.2(f) (p0695) covers actual or alleged third-party IP infringement "by the Product or by either Party in performing its duties or obligations hereunder", so we indemnify SFJ (and SFJ's investors) even for infringement caused by SFJ's own performance. That is a one-way IP indemnity for the counterparty's activities, which fails the fallback (Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions) and sits in walk-away territory under the detection guidance. Minimal fix: add an IP-infringement limb to SFJ's indemnity limited to SFJ's, its Affiliates' and Permitted Third Parties' performance, and narrow limb (f) of our indemnity to PB-side activities, leaving Product-based infringement (which we own) with us.

proposal.summary: Add SFJ IP-infringement indemnity for its own performance and narrow PB's outbound IP indemnity to PB-side activities
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added an SFJ indemnity for third-party IP infringement claims arising from SFJ's own performance, and narrowed our indemnity in Section 12.1.2(f) so we no longer cover infringement caused by SFJ's activities. Our playbook does not permit an IP indemnity that runs one way only from us; if helpful we can instead make limb (f) reciprocal, each Party covering its own performance.
